wins.need: Recharging a 5 kWh home battery from a large rooftop or ground-mount solar array
wins.claim: Takes twice the solar input of the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus and more than 2.6 times that of the Anker SOLIX S5000
wins.figure: TITAN 5000 Plus: 4 kW × 2 inputs, 40-450V, 16 A, so 8,000 W in total. Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus: up to 4,000 W. Anker SOLIX S5000: 3,000 W max (1,000 W + 2,000 W).
wins.source: https://www.ecoflow.com/us/ecoflow-titan-series/specs ; https://www.jackery.com/products/jackery-explorer-5000-plus (store listing text, read with our storecheck search) ; https://www.ankersolix.com/s5000
wins.who: Maker spec pages (EcoFlow US, Jackery US, Anker SOLIX)

wins.need: Running 240V central AC and a whole house at the same time
wins.claim: Rated AC output equals the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus and is 60% higher than the Anker SOLIX S5000. With solar connected it rises to 10 kW, which neither rival lists.
wins.figure: TITAN 5000 Plus: 7,200 W at 120V/240V, 'up to 10 kW with PV input'. Jackery: 7,200 W rated. Anker S5000: 4,500 W rated. Arithmetic: 7,200 / 4,500 = 1.6.
wins.who: Maker spec pages. pv magazine USA also reports '7.2 kW at 120/240 V, rising to 10 kW when hooked in to a solar supply' (https://pv-magazine-usa.com/2026/10/14/ecoflow-launches-5-30-kwh-residential-storage-system/)

wins.need: Charging fast from the grid or a generator before a storm
wins.claim: Accepts more AC charging power than the Anker SOLIX S5000
wins.figure: TITAN 5000 Plus: AC input '10 kW max' through the 5P8 port (1,800 W through CP20). Anker S5000: 4,500 W max at 240V, 1,800 W at 120V.

wins.need: Building up to about 30 kWh over time
wins.claim: Arithmetic: each added battery costs less per Wh than Jackery's 5000 Plus battery pack
wins.figure: EcoFlow TITAN Battery 5kWh $2,299, about $0.46/Wh. Jackery Battery Pack 5000 Plus $2,599 / 5,040 Wh = $0.52/Wh. Arithmetic for 30 kWh: TITAN 5000 Plus $3,699 (Amazon) + 5 × $2,299 = $15,194. Jackery $3,499 + 5 × $2,599 = $16,494.
wins.who: Arithmetic on maker-store and Amazon prices read the same day

wins.need: Lower weight among 7.2 kW 5 kWh units
wins.claim: Lighter than the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus at the same rated output
wins.figure: TITAN 5000 Plus: 55 kg (121.3 lb). Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus: 134.5 lb (61 kg).
wins.who: EcoFlow spec page. The Jackery weight is Backup Power Hub quoting Jackery's US page (Jackery's own page returned HTTP 429).
EcoFlow spec page (maker rating, not measured by anyone else)

weak.claim: Costs more per Wh than both 5 kWh rivals
weak.figure: Arithmetic on Amazon prices: TITAN 5000 Plus $3,699 / 5,017.6 Wh = $0.74/Wh. Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus $3,499 / 5,040 Wh = $0.69/Wh. Anker SOLIX S5000 $2,949 / 5,024 Wh = $0.59/Wh.

weak.claim: Slower switchover to battery than both rivals
weak.figure: TITAN 5000 Plus: UPS ≤20 ms. Anker SOLIX S5000: ≤10 ms. Jackery says 'True 0ms UPS switching'; Backup Power Hub, quoting Jackery, says this is 0 ms on the 5-20 outlets, up to 3,600 W.

weak.claim: Not portable: rated for dry indoor use only, with no wheels, while the Anker S5000 is a lighter wheeled unit
weak.figure: TITAN 5000 Plus: IP20, 121.3 lb, wheels: 'None, floor-standing' (Backup Power Hub). Anker S5000: 97 lb, wheels shown on its spec diagram.

weak.claim: Has few outlets on the unit itself, so plugging devices straight in is limited
weak.figure: Off-grid outlets: NEMA 5-20R × 2 and NEMA L14-50R × 1 (EcoFlow). Jackery 5000 Plus: 4 × NEMA 5-20, 14-50 + L14-30R, 2 × USB-C 100 W, 2 × USB-A, car socket (Backup Power Hub, quoting Jackery).

weak.claim: Expands to half the maximum capacity of Jackery's system
weak.figure: TITAN: 5 kWh × 6 = 30 kWh maximum. Jackery: expandable up to 60 kWh (two 5000 Plus units in parallel with 10 battery packs, 60.48 kWh).

weak.claim: Whole-home backup needs a panel and installation on top of the unit. The 10 kW figure needs solar connected.
weak.figure: pv magazine USA: '$3,000 range standalone' or '$7,000 range including the home panel and installation'. SHP10 installation labor about $1,200. EcoFlow store: 'AC coupling with an existing rooftop solar system requires the Smart Home Panel 10 (SHP10 240V) and a CT sensor'.

wins_for: Homes with, or planning, more than 4 kW of solar that want one 240V battery to take all of it. 8,000 W solar input is double the Jackery 5000 Plus and the non-Plus TITAN 5000 (4 kW, one MPPT, per pv magazine USA).
Whole-home backup that has to start 240V central AC alongside other loads: 7,200 W, up to 10 kW with PV, used with the Smart Home Panel 10.
Buyers who expect to grow to about 30 kWh. By arithmetic the add-on batteries cost less per Wh than Jackery's.
not_for: Lowest cost per Wh for a 5 kWh, 240V backup: the Anker SOLIX S5000 ($0.59/Wh on Amazon) or Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus ($0.69/Wh) win.
Moving the battery around, camping or RV use: the IP20 rating means indoor only and it has no wheels. The Anker S5000 is 97 lb with wheels.
Computers or medical devices that cannot tolerate any switchover gap: the Jackery 5000 Plus offers 0 ms UPS on its 5-20 outlets and the Anker S5000 ≤10 ms, against ≤20 ms here.
Homes with no solar or under 4 kW of solar: the 10 kW boost and second 4 kW MPPT do nothing for them. The TITAN 5000 has the same 7.2 kW for $3,199 on Amazon, $500 less.
Plug-in use without a panel install: it has only two 5-20R outlets and one L14-50R. The Jackery 5000 Plus has many more on the unit.

rivals.price: $3,499 at Amazon (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DFGLG35L, read 2026-11-15). $3,499 at the Jackery store, pre-order shipping Nov 28 (https://www.jackery.com/products/jackery-explorer-5000-plus, read 2026-11-15).
rivals.where_it_beats_ours: Cheaper per Wh ($0.69 vs $0.74). 0 ms UPS on 5-20 outlets. Expands to 60 kWh with two units. Wheels and many more outlets on the unit.
$750 cheaper ($0.59/Wh). 97 lb with wheels. ≤10 ms UPS. Anker rates it 10,000 cycles. It loses on output (4,500 W vs 7,200 W) and solar input (3,000 W vs 8,000 W).
$500 less for the same 7.2 kW. The trade-off is 4 kW solar through one MPPT instead of 8 kW (pv magazine USA, read 2026-11-15).

EcoFlow US store price: storecheck search showed $50 with compare-at $12,696, which looks like a deposit or placeholder, not a unit price. The product page and the storecheck product read returned HTTP 429 every time, so I could not see what the $50 is.
Independent measurements: none found. Backup Power Hub states no independent review of the TITAN had been published as of 2026-11-01. Every TITAN figure above is EcoFlow's rating.
Cycle life: not listed on EcoFlow's US spec page; I looked for it there and in pv magazine USA.
Certifications on the spec page: not listed there. EcoFlow's store search text says 'UL 9540A tested and UL 9540 certified'; the product page itself could not be opened (HTTP 429).
Return window, Amazon or EcoFlow: the EcoFlow return-policy URL gave 404 and Amazon was walled.
Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus weight, outlets and cycle life: taken from Backup Power Hub quoting Jackery, because Jackery's product page returned HTTP 429.
Anker SOLIX S5000 warranty: the spec page only links to a separate policy page, which I did not open.
EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra as a rival: Amazon search returned nothing and the EcoFlow store was rate-limited, so it is left out.
